text:
Brett Kulak has become a load-bearing wall in Colorado this week. With Cale Makar out about two weeks and Josh Manson on long-term injured reserve, the Avalanche are two regular defensemen short, and the 32-year-old is playing about 19 to 20 minutes a night, up more than a minute over his last ten games.

He isn't there for offense. He has 5 assists and no goals in 21 games, and his chance totals say the zero is about right for a defenseman who shoots from distance. The concern is the five-on-five share: Colorado has 47.9% of the expected goals, the quality of chances, with him on the ice, about seven points worse than without him. Evolving-Hockey had him around replacement level last season, too.

What Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking likes is the skating game: half his exits leave the zone with possession, and 28% of his shots come off the rush, well above a typical defenseman's 17%. On a thinned blue line, the clean exits matter more than the points.
